tools.name: get_note
tools.title: Get note
tools.description:
Fetches a note by GUID. Returns the title, body (ENML), parent notebook GUID, version, timestamps, trash state (`active` / `deleted`), plus the satellite payloads ENML cannot express on its own — tasks, tags, resource manifest, and selected note attributes — in `structuredContent`.

The body is returned in ENML (Evernote's XML dialect). To change the body, call `edit_note` with a `mode` (append/prepend/replace) and a small ENML `content` fragment — you do not resend the whole body. For `replace`, copy a byte-exact, unique snippet of this ENML as the `find` anchor.

Important — ENML is not the full story:
- Task groups appear in ENML only as a per-group placeholder div (`--en-task-group:true`); the task entities themselves live in `structuredContent.tasks[]` as a lightweight summary (`id`, `label`, `status`, `dueDate`). Read those fields from there, not from the ENML. For a task's `description`, `priority`, `flag`, `recurring` state, or assignee, call `get_task(taskId)`. To **edit** tasks, use the dedicated tools — `create_task`, `update_task` (status changes are an `update_task` field), `delete_task` — never via `edit_note` and ENML splicing.
- `<en-media>` references carry only the resource hash. Filename, mime type, and size live in `structuredContent.resources` — use those to decide whether the bytes are worth fetching via `get_attachment`.

Prerequisites: call `search_notes` or `semantic_search` first if you don't already have a note GUID.

noteId.description: GUID of the note to fetch.

tools.name: search_notes
tools.title: Search notes
tools.description:
Searches notes using Evernote's search grammar — the same query language as the Evernote app's search bar. Use for deterministic, structured queries; for meaning-based queries use `semantic_search` instead. Returns note GUIDs, titles, snippets, and timestamps — follow up with `get_note(noteId)` for full content.

Empty `query` lists all active notes (trash excluded). Pass `intrash:true` to list only trashed notes, or `intrash:false` for active only. `intrash:` accepts only `true`/`false` — there is no single-query way to list active and trashed together.

Common operators: `tag:work`, `notebook:"My Notebook"`, `intitle:meeting`, `created:day-7`, `updated:day-1`, `any: a b` (OR across the following terms — the space after `any:` is required). Quote multi-word values (`tag:"to read"`). Combine with spaces (AND) or `OR` (when `fullBooleanSearch` is true).

Date-relative operators (`created:day-7`, `updated:day-1`) need `clientTimeZone` to resolve correctly.

query.description: Evernote search-grammar string. Empty string lists all active notes (trash excluded), matching the Evernote app's default "All Notes" view; pass `intrash:true` to list only trashed notes, or `intrash:false` for active only (`intrash:` accepts only `true`/`false` — there is no single-query way to list active and trashed together). Common operators: `tag:work` (notes with tag), `notebook:"My Notebook"` (notes in notebook), `intitle:meeting` (substring in title), `created:day-7` (created in the last 7 days, needs `clientTimeZone` to be accurate), `updated:day-1`, `any: a b` (OR across the following terms — the space after `any:` is required). Quote multi-word values: `tag:"to read"`. Combine with spaces (AND) or `OR` (when `fullBooleanSearch` is true). Use this tool for deterministic / structured queries ("last 10 notes", "notes in notebook X", "notes with tag K"). For meaning-based queries use `semantic_search` instead.

clientTimeZone.description: IANA time zone (e.g. `America/New_York`). Required for date-relative operators like `created:day-7` / `updated:day-1` to resolve correctly. Defaults to UTC.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of notes to return (1–100). Default 10.

startIndex.description: 0-based offset into the result list. Combine with `maxResults` to paginate. Use `totalResultCount` from a previous response to decide whether to keep paging.

sortBy.description: Sort field. `updated` (default) for recency; `created` for original date; `relevance` for search-score ranking (only useful with a non-empty query); `title` for alphabetical.

ascending.description: When true, sort ascending (oldest first / A→Z). Default false (newest first / Z→A).

fullBooleanSearch.description: When true, `AND` / `OR` / `NOT` in the query are interpreted as boolean operators (matches the Evernote search bar behavior). When false, those words are literal. Default true.

tools.name: search_notebooks
tools.title: Search notebooks
tools.description:
Lists or searches the user's notebooks by name. Empty `query` returns all notebooks; pass a substring to filter (case-insensitive, ranked exact > prefix > substring; ties alphabetical).

Pass `defaultOnly: true` to return only the user's formal default notebook (the one a note created without a target lands in) — at most one hit, and an empty result means no formal default is configured. With `defaultOnly`, `query`, `maxResults`, and `sortBy` are ignored.

Returns each notebook's GUID, label, `stack` (or null), `primaryAccess` (OWNED / SHARED / WORKSPACE / BUSINESS), `workspaceId` + `workspaceName` (the Space the notebook belongs to, or null when it isn't in one), and a ready-to-use `searchFilter` (`nbGuid:"<id>"`) that can be dropped into `search_notes`. Use `workspaceId` / `workspaceName` to tell which Space a notebook lives in and to group notebooks by Space; the `workspaceId` is also what `create_notebook` and `create_note` take to place a new notebook/note inside that Space.

Use this to resolve a notebook name to a GUID before calling `create_note`, `move_notes`, or `rename_notebook`. To search note **content**, use `search_notes` (deterministic) or `semantic_search` (meaning-based).

query.description: Notebook name substring to match (case-insensitive). Empty string (default) lists all the user's notebooks, sorted by `sortBy`. When non-empty, matches are ranked: exact > prefix > substring; ties break alphabetically. Matching is name-only — `notebook:` / `tag:` / other note-grammar operators have no effect here.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of notebooks to return (1–100). Default 10. Bump to e.g. 100 to approximate the full list view in the Evernote app's notebook list.

sortBy.description: Sort field, applied when `query` is empty (or after rank-by-match when `query` is non-empty). `name` (default) sorts alphabetically A→Z. `updated` sorts by most-recently-touched first (notebook version DESC) — useful for surfacing the notebooks the user has been working with lately. Caveat: `updated` reflects changes to the notebook itself (e.g. renames or notebook-metadata changes) and may not reflect edits to the notes inside it. `updated` is independent of any substring filter.

defaultOnly.description: Return only the user's formal default notebook — the one a note created without a target notebook lands in. At most one hit is returned, and an empty result means no formal default is configured. When true, `query`, `maxResults`, and `sortBy` are ignored.

tools.name: search_tags
tools.title: Search tags
tools.description:
Lists or searches the user's tags by name. Empty `query` returns all tags; pass a substring to filter — matched case-insensitively server-side across your whole tag set, then ranked exact > prefix > substring (ties alphabetical).

Returns each tag's GUID, label, and a ready-to-use `searchFilter` (`tagGuid:"<id>"`) that can be dropped into `search_notes`.

At most 500 matching tags are fetched per call (a hard upstream cap, no paging). When the query matches more than 500 tags, the tail is dropped, `totalResultCount` saturates at 500, and `isLastPage` is `false` — so `totalResultCount: 500` with `isLastPage: false` means "500 or more", not exactly 500. To see tags beyond the cap, refine `query` to a narrower substring so it matches fewer than 500.

Use this to resolve a tag name to a GUID before calling `create_note`, `edit_note`, `update_note_tags`, or `edit_tag`. To search notes carrying a tag, use `search_notes` with `tag:"<name>"`.

query.description: Tag name substring to match (case-insensitive). Empty string (default) lists all the user's tags, sorted by `sortBy`. When non-empty, the substring is matched server-side across the user's entire tag set (so matches aren't limited to recently-touched tags), then ranked: exact > prefix > substring; ties break alphabetically. Matching is name-only — `notebook:` / `tag:` / other note-grammar operators have no effect here.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of tags to return (1–100). Default 10. Bump to e.g. 100 to approximate the full list view in the Evernote app's tag panel.

sortBy.description: Sort field, applied when `query` is empty (or after rank-by-match when `query` is non-empty). `name` (default) sorts alphabetically A→Z. `updated` sorts by most-recently-touched first (tag version DESC) — useful for surfacing the tags the user has been working with lately. `updated` is independent of any substring filter.

tools.name: get_attachment
tools.title: Get attachment download URL
tools.description:
Returns a short-lived, pre-signed HTTPS URL to download an Evernote attachment (referenced by `<en-media hash=...>` in note ENML). The URL points straight at the file bytes and can be fetched directly — no Evernote auth header, no follow-up call. It expires after a short window (see `expiresAt`), so fetch it promptly rather than storing it. Works on owned, shared, and business notes — the URL is only issued if you can read the note.

Tip: `get_note`'s `structuredContent.resources` already lists every attachment on the note with its hash, mime, and filename, so you typically know which hash you want before calling this tool.

noteId.description: GUID of the note that owns the attachment. Same shape as `get_note`'s `noteId`.

hash.description: The attachment's content hash (lowercase MD5), as it appears in the `hash` attribute of an `<en-media>` tag inside the note's ENML.
